speaker: Doctor
text: The urinalysis shows trace protein but is otherwise clear of infection, blood, or white blood cells. Since infection is unlikely, do you experience pain or burning specifically at the start of urination, or is it constant throughout? Also, have you noticed any changes in your urine volume, such as urgency or difficulty emptying your bladder?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
Thank you for those details; the symptom of discomfort relieved by voiding combined with dyspareunia is highly suggestive of interstitial cystitis/bladder pain syndrome. Given your age and the chronic nature of these symptoms, have you noticed any pelvic pressure or pain in your lower abdomen as well?

The pelvic exam confirms bladder tenderness with no signs of infection or structural abnormalities, and the ultrasound rules out significant retention. To further characterize your bladder wall inflammation, would you mind reporting any visible "blue spots" on your bladder surface, and have you ever noticed clear mucus plugs in your urine?

The cystoscopy results are reassuringly normal, which helps rule out Hunner's ulcers or carcinoma, though your symptoms of bladder pain relieved by voiding and dyspareunia are very characteristic. Given the negative workup for infection, stones, and structural issues, have you had any difficulty initiating urination or a sensation of incomplete emptying?
